name: E-commerce and D2C brands

sector.title: Digital economy, social and public sector

shape_facts: Main storefront (Shopify, WooCommerce, custom) and whether they also sell on marketplaces or Instagram.
Rough order volume per day or month and average order size band (only if they volunteer it).
Share of COD versus prepaid, and which couriers they use.
Own warehouse/home stock, third-party fulfilment, or made-to-order.
Markets served: Pakistan only, UAE/GCC, Canada, or cross-border.
Team size and who handles customer service, packing and ads.
Whether they manufacture, source locally, or import.
scope_rule: pi notes operational problems across the order-to-cash chain: order confirmation, stock, packing, couriers, returns, COD remittance, ad tracking, customer service and reporting. It does not give tax advice (sales tax registration, VAT, GST/HST, customs duties), consumer-law or legal advice on refund policies, or advice on payment-gateway compliance. It never asks for customer names, phone numbers, addresses, card details or store/admin passwords, and records customers only as “a customer” or “repeat buyers”. It does not help with fake reviews, fake order inflation or under-declaring shipments.

vocabulary.COD: cash on delivery; customer pays the rider.
vocabulary.RTO: return to origin; parcel refused or undelivered and sent back.
vocabulary.Remittance / payment cycle: courier transferring collected COD money to the seller.
vocabulary.Order confirmation call: calling or WhatsApping the buyer before dispatch.
vocabulary.ROAS: revenue per unit of ad spend.
vocabulary.Fake order: order placed with no intention to receive.
vocabulary.Restock alert: notice when an item is back.
vocabulary.Bundle / deal: grouped products at a set price.

returns/rto: Roughly how many parcels come back out of every ten?
Do you confirm orders before sending them?
Is it certain cities or certain products?
cod cash: How long after delivery does the money usually land?
How do you check each payment against orders today?
stock: Where do you keep your stock count — Shopify, Excel, or in your head?
How often do you find the website and the shelf don’t match?
ads: Which channels are you spending on right now?
How do you decide an ad is working?
margin: When you think about one order, what costs do you subtract?
Do you know which products lose money once returns are counted?
customer service: How many “where’s my order” messages do you get a day?
channels: Where do orders come in from?
How do they end up in one list for packing?
packing: How do packers know what goes in each parcel?
How do you find out a wrong item was sent?
reporting: What numbers do you look at every morning?
How long does it take to put them together?
growth: What is the next big thing you’re planning — new market, new range, more volume?
What worries you most about it?

seasons: Pakistan: Ramadan and Eid ul-Fitr (biggest fashion, gifting and food peak), Eid ul-Adha, wedding season (roughly November to March), 11.11 and 12.12 sales, Black Friday/“White Friday”, summer lawn launches (spring), winter collections (October onward), 14 August, school-start season. UAE: Ramadan and Eid, Dubai Shopping Festival (December–January), White Friday/Yellow Friday, 11.11, Back-to-School (late August), summer slowdown with residents travelling, National Day (2 December). Canada: Black Friday/Cyber Monday, Boxing Day, holiday season, back-to-school, Valentine’s and Mother’s Day for gifting. Ramadan moves about ten to eleven days earlier each year.
care: Never collect customer phone numbers, addresses, card details or Shopify/courier logins; ask for patterns, not records.
Do not advise on sales tax, VAT, GST/HST, customs declaration or import duty; note “unsure about tax registration” as compliance_admin/tax_filing_effort only.
Refuse requests to generate fake reviews, inflate order counts, use competitor branding or under-declare parcel values.
Do not give legal views on refund/return policy wording or consumer-protection rules.
Fake-order and fraud discussions: note the operational pattern; do not help profile or blacklist individuals by identity.
If an owner mentions a rider or customer being threatened or harmed during delivery, point to emergency services first.
Do not promise lower RTO or higher ROAS; never quote benchmark rates.
Founders often blur personal and business money; note cash_flow_tight without giving financial advice.
build_ideas: Single order inbox pulling Shopify/WooCommerce, Instagram DMs and marketplace orders into one packing queue.
WhatsApp order-confirmation flow that messages each COD buyer, records confirm/cancel, and holds unconfirmed orders.
COD remittance reconciler: upload courier settlement sheets, auto-match to orders, list unpaid and short-paid parcels.
RTO tracker by city, courier, product and confirmation status, showing where returns cluster.
Per-order profit view combining product cost, shipping, payment fees, returns and allocated ad spend.
Live stock sync between warehouse count and storefront with low-stock alerts on best-sellers.
Pick-and-pack checklist with barcode or SKU scan to catch wrong items before sealing.
“Where is my order” WhatsApp bot that reads courier tracking and replies automatically.
Repeat-buyer and win-back lists (without exposing personal data in reports) with campaign scheduling.
Daily owner summary on WhatsApp: orders, dispatched, delivered, returned, cash due from couriers.
Returns intake log: condition check, restock or write-off, refund status.
Seasonal buying planner using last year’s sales by SKU around Eid, sales events and launches.
Ad spend versus orders dashboard linking campaign UTM tags to actual delivered (not just placed) orders.

exchange.text: Bhai sab se bara masla returns ka hai. COD parcels wapas aa jate hain aur double shipping lagti hai.
Samajh gaya, yeh kaafi mehnga par jata hai. Noted — COD parcels zyada wapas aa rahe hain aur dono taraf ki shipping lag rahi hai. Kya aap order bhejne se pehle customer se confirm karte hain?
Karte hain, lekin ek hi larki karti hai calls, aadhe miss ho jate hain.
Noted — confirmation ek bande par hai aur kaafi orders bina confirm ke chale jate hain. Zyada returns kisi khaas sheher ya product se aate hain, ya har jagah se?
Karachi se kam, interior Sindh aur Punjab ke chhote sheheron se zyada.
